name: Muharram
intro:
The month of Muharram is a month full of events, the greatest of which is the martyrdom of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH).
Events took place on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 19, 20, 23, 25, 26, 28 and 29 of this month, most of them related to the tragedy of Karbala.
Imam Husayn's (PBUH) approach to Karbala, his entry into that land and his letter to the people of Kufa, the arrival of Umar ibn Sa'd in Karbala, the fatwa of Shurayh the judge for the killing of Imam Husayn (PBUH) and the massing of Yazid's army, Imam Husayn's (PBUH) meeting with Ibn Sa'd, the denial of water to Imam Husayn (PBUH), the siege of the tents in Karbala, the arrival of a safe-conduct letter for the sons of Umm al-Banin (PBUH), the request to delay the battle, the arrival of fresh troops in Karbala, Imam Husayn's (PBUH) address to his companions, the Imam's (PBUH) words with his household, and the words of Zaynab al-Kubra (PBUH) with Imam Husayn (PBUH) - all of these are stages of the Karbala tragedy that took place in the month of Muharram before the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH).
The martyrdom of Sayyid al-Shuhada Imam Husayn (PBUH), the martyrdom of the Moon of the Banu Hashim, Hazrat Abbas (PBUH), the martyrdom of Hazrat Ali Akbar (PBUH), the martyrdom of Qasim ibn Hasan (PBUH), the martyrdom of Bab al-Hawa'ij Ali Asghar (PBUH), the martyrdom of Abdullah ibn Hasan (PBUH), the martyrdom of Habib ibn Mazahir al-Asadi and Muslim ibn Awsajah, the martyrdom of Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi and Jawn, the servant of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, the martyrdom of the faithful companions of Imam Husayn (PBUH), and the martyrdom of Wahb's wife at the hands of Shimr's servant are manifestations of the greatest record of martyrdom, which was realized in the month of Muharram.
The arrival of Dhuljanah with a blood-stained mane at the tent of the Fatimid women, the mourning, wailing and weeping of the women of the sanctuary over Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH) and his children, the plundering of belongings from the tents of Imam Husayn (PBUH), the stripping of clothes and armor from the pure bodies of the martyrs of Karbala, the burning of the tents of the Family of God, the flight of the Fatimid and Alawid women into the desert, the martyrdom of young girls beside the tents, and the severing of the pure heads of Imam Husayn (PBUH), his household and his companions are events that took place after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH), all in the month of Muharram.
The pure head of Imam Husayn (PBUH) in Khawli's oven in Kufa, the departure of the caravan of captives from Karbala, the departure of the household of Imam Husayn (PBUH) toward Kufa, the burial of the martyrs of Karbala, the entry of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) into Kufa, the captivity of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) in Ibn Ziyad's court, the captivity of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) in the prison of Kufa, the news of the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH) in Medina and Syria, and the martyrdom of Abdullah ibn Afif are events that Kufa witnessed in the month of Muharram. Afterwards the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) were paraded through the cities of Iraq and Syria, and it was in this same month that they reached Syria.
Other events also occurred in the month of Muharram, some before and some after the Karbala tragedy. The affair of Shi'b Abi Talib (PBUH), the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa', the first collection of zakat, the writing of the accursed scroll, and the death of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman took place in Muharram before the Karbala events.
The uprising of the people of Medina against Yazid after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH), the killing of Ibn Ziyad, the deaths of Umm Salamah and Maria al-Qibtiyya (two wives of the Messenger of God (SAWW)), the martyrdom of Imam Sajjad (PBUH), the uprising of Zayd ibn Ali ibn Husayn (PBUH), the Ashura words of Imam Reza (PBUH), and the exile of Imam Jawad (PBUH) are events that occurred in Muharram after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH). God willing, the uprising of Imam Mahdi (PBUH) will also take place in the month of Muharram, on the day of Ashura.
This was a summary of the events that took place in the sacred month of Muharram, which we will cover in detail in this section.

events.title: The Beginning of the Husayni Days
events.text:
The first day of the month of grief and sorrow of the Family of Muhammad (PBUT), when all the prophets, angels, Shi'a and friends of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) are in mourning. It can be said that this is the month of grief and sorrow for the entire world, because every year, from the first of Muharram until the day of Ashura, the torn shirt of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH) is hung down from the Throne of God toward the earth, and the grief and sorrow of the world takes hold.
It is also the beginning of the mourning gatherings for Hazrat Aba Abdillah (PBUH), which acquaint people with their religious beliefs; people carry the teachings of their faith from the Husayniyyas, takiyyas and mosques to the homes of their minds and hearts as a gift. Taking part in the mourning ceremonies for Imam Husayn (PBUH) and weeping for him is among our duties in the era of the Occultation of Imam Zaman (PBUH).
sources: Khasa'is al-Zaynabiyya: p. 49, 19th distinctive feature.

events.title: The Affair of Shi'b Abi Talib (PBUH)
events.text:
Following the growing power of Islam after the Prophet's (SAWW) mission, the Quraysh wrote a pact, agreeing in it not to speak with the Banu Hashim, not to share meals or sit with them, and not to trade with them; and they pressured them so that they would hand the Prophet (SAWW) over to the Quraysh in order to kill him. Hazrat Abu Talib (PBUH) took the Banu Hashim to a valley that was attributed to him, fortified its surroundings, and girded his loins night and day to protect the life of the Prophet (SAWW).
At night that Hazrat would circle, sword in hand, around the candle of the Prophet's (SAWW) being like a moth, saying: “As long as I am alive, I will not cease helping him.” Several times each night he changed the Prophet's (SAWW) sleeping place and had his dearest son, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), sleep in the Prophet's place, and by day he assigned his own sons and his brothers' sons to guard him. The time they spent in the Shi'b was extremely hard on him and on the Muslims, to the point that at night the people living around the Shi'b could hear the crying of the hungry children of the Banu Hashim.
After two years and a few months, God appointed the termite, and it destroyed the pact except for the names of God that were in it. Hazrat Abu Talib (PBUH) informed the disbelievers of this, and upon seeing such a miracle they abandoned their decision and the Banu Hashim returned to their homes.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 9. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 7.

events.title: The Battle of Dhat al-Riqa'
events.text: In the fourth year of the Hijra - at the instigation of the Quraysh disbelievers - a war broke out between the Muslims and the tribes living around Medina who intended to besiege it. The Prophet (SAWW) went out of Medina with 400 or 790 men. In this expedition the Prophet (SAWW) performed the Prayer of Fear (Salat al-Khawf), and the fighting lasted three days until their evil was repelled. According to one account, this event took place on 15 Jumada al-Ula.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 45. Tawdih al-Maqasid: pp. 2-3. Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 98.

events.title: The First Collection of Zakat
events.text: On the first of Muharram, the Prophet (SAWW) for the first time sent officials to the surroundings of Medina to collect zakat and alms.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 42. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 15.

events.title: Imam Husayn (PBUH) on the Road to Karbala
events.text: On the first of Muharram, Imam Husayn (PBUH) stopped at Qasr Bani Muqatil and invited Ubaydullah ibn Hurr al-Ju'fi to help him, but he did not respond and later regretted it.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 81.

events.title: The Uprising of the People of Medina Against Yazid
events.text: On this day in the year 63 AH, the people of Medina set out to rise against Yazid. The matter began when a group of the people of Medina, led by Abdullah ibn Handhala, went to Syria and saw Yazid's court, his drinking, gambling and dog-play, and returned to Medina and informed the people of the corruption of the Umayyad court. Upon hearing this news, everyone agreed to depose Yazid, and under Abdullah's leadership they rose against Yazid and expelled the Umayyads living in Medina. When the Syrian army learned of this uprising, it marched toward Medina, and the incident of Harra took place.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 49.

events.title: The Ashura Words of Imam Reza (PBUH)
events.text:
On the first of Muharram, Rayyan ibn Shabib came into the presence of Imam Reza (PBUH). The Hazrat said to him: O son of Shabib, the Arabs in the Age of Ignorance considered fighting unlawful during the days of Muharram; but this nation destroyed the sanctity of this month and did not honor the sanctity of the Prophet (SAWW). In this month they considered our blood lawful, violated our sanctity, took our children and women captive, set our tents on fire and plundered our belongings, and did not observe the respect due to the Messenger of God (SAWW) with regard to us.
Indeed, the day of the martyrdom of Husayn (PBUH) wounded our eyelids, made our tears flow, burned our hearts, humiliated our dear one in the land of Karbala, and bequeathed to us affliction and calamity until the Day of Recompense. So let those who weep, weep for Husayn (PBUH), for weeping for him wipes away great sins.
O son of Shabib, if you want to weep over anything, weep for Husayn ibn Ali (PBUH), for they slaughtered him as a sheep is slaughtered, and with him eighteen men of his household were killed who had no like or equal on the earth. The seven heavens and the earths wept at his martyrdom. Four thousand angels came on the day of Ashura to help him and saw that he had been martyred. So they were commanded to stay, disheveled and dusty, at the vicinity of that pure grave until Hazrat Qa'im (PBUH) rises, and to be among his helpers, and their slogan is “Ya la-tharat al-Husayn” (O avengers of Husayn).
O son of Shabib, if you wish to be with us in the high ranks of Paradise, be sad at our sadness and happy at our happiness; and hold fast to our wilayah (guardianship), for if a person loves a stone, God Almighty will raise him with that very stone....
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 98, p. 102; vol. 14, p. 164. Amali of Saduq: p. 111. Iqbal: p. 544. Uyun Akhbar al-Reza (PBUH): vol. 1, p. 233.

events.title: The Entry of Imam Husayn (PBUH) into Karbala
events.text:
According to the well-known view, on this day in the year 61 AH our master and lord Hazrat Aba Abdillah al-Husayn, Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH), entered Karbala al-Mu'alla together with his household and companions.
There, the Hazrat's horse would not move. The Imam (PBUH) asked: What is the name of this land? They said: “Ghadiriyya.” He asked for its other name; they said: “Shati' al-Furat.” He said: Does it have another name? They said: It is also called “Karbala.” At this the Hazrat sighed deeply, wept intensely and said: “Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min al-karb wa al-bala” (O God, I seek refuge in You from distress and affliction). By God, this is the land of Karbala. By God, here they will kill our men! By God, here they will take our women and children captive! By God, here the veil of our sanctity will be torn! O noble men, dismount, for this is the place of our graves....
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 84. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 24. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 89. Manaqib of Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 105. Jala' al-Uyun: p. 379. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 1, p. 285.
From Medina to Medina: p. 326. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 142.

events.title: Imam Husayn's (PBUH) Letter to the People of Kufa
events.text: On this day Imam Husayn (PBUH) wrote a letter to the notables of Kufa and gave it to Qays ibn Mushir al-Saydawi to deliver to Kufa. The agents seized Qays on the way, and after he spoke against Yazid and Ibn Ziyad, they martyred him.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 41.

events.title: The Arrival of Umar ibn Sa'd in Karbala
events.text: On this day Umar ibn Sa'd, with six or nine thousand horsemen, entered Karbala to kill the son of the Prophet (SAWW), set up a camp opposite him and pitched tents. It has also been reported that Ibn Sa'd's arrival in Karbala took place on the fourth day.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 40. From Medina to Medina: p. 343. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 1, p. 301. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 143.

events.title: The Fatwa of Shurayh the Judge for the Killing of Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text: On this day in 61 AH, Ibn Ziyad, citing a fatwa he had obtained from Shurayh the judge, delivered a sermon in the Mosque of Kufa and incited the people to kill Imam Husayn (PBUH).
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 124.

events.title: Habib ibn Mazahir Seeks Help from the Banu Asad
events.text: On the night of the sixth, Habib ibn Mazahir al-Asadi, with the permission of Imam Husayn (PBUH), went to the Banu Asad tribe to bring supporters and help. The Asadis accepted and set out, but spies informed Umar ibn Sa'd, and he sent a group to stop them. A clash therefore took place in which a number of the Banu Asad were martyred or wounded and the rest were forced to flee, and Habib came into the presence of the Hazrat and reported what had happened.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 149. From Medina to Medina: pp. 368-370.

events.title: The First Blockade of the Euphrates in Karbala
events.text: According to one account, on this day Umar ibn Sa'd sent the vile Shabath ibn Rib'i, with three thousand ruthless men, beating drums and kettledrums, to the banks of the Euphrates, and they besieged its surroundings.
sources: From Medina to Medina: p. 360.

events.title: The Massing of Yazid's Army in Karbala
events.text: On this day a great army gathered to fight Hazrat Aba Abdillah (PBUH).
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 153.

events.title: Imam Husayn's (PBUH) Meeting with Ibn Sa'd
events.text: On the night of the seventh, Imam Husayn (PBUH) met and conversed with the accursed Umar ibn Sa'd. Khawli ibn Yazid al-Asbahi, who bore intense enmity toward the Imam (PBUH), reported the matter to Ibn Ziyad, and that accursed one wrote a letter to Umar ibn Sa'd, warned him against these meetings, and issued the order to cut off the water.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 63. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 1, p. 315.

events.title: The Denial of Water to Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text: On this day water was cut off from the household of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH), since a letter from Ibn Ziyad arrived with the content: do not let even a single drop of water reach them. Amr ibn al-Hajjaj al-Zubaydi, with four thousand archers, was appointed to guard the Euphrates so that no water at all would be carried to the camp of the son of the Prophet (SAWW).
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 153. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 146.

events.title: Water Scarcity in the Husayni Tents
events.text: On this day water became unavailable in the tents of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH).
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 81. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 2, p. 154.

events.title: The Siege of the Tents in Karbala
events.text: Imam Sadiq (PBUH) said: Tasu'a was the day on which Husayn (PBUH) and his companions were besieged in Karbala and the army of Syria gathered to fight him; the son of Marjana and Umar ibn Sa'd were pleased because of the large army and forces that had been assembled for them, and they considered that Hazrat and his companions weak and were certain that no helper would come to him and that the people of Iraq would not support him.
sources: Kafi: vol. 4, p. 147.

events.title: The Arrival of the Safe-Conduct Letter for the Sons of Umm al-Banin (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day the accursed Shimr brought a safe-conduct letter for Hazrat Abbas (PBUH) and his brothers. That wretch drew close to the dignified tents of Hazrat Aba Abdillah (PBUH) and cried out: “Ayna banu ukhtina” (Where are the sons of our sister?)! But those noble ones did not answer. Imam Husayn (PBUH) said: Answer him, even though he is a transgressor. Hazrat Abbas (PBUH) replied: What are you saying? Shimr said: I have brought you a safe-conduct from the commander. Do not get yourselves killed for the sake of Husayn (PBUH).
Hazrat Abbas (PBUH) said in a loud voice: “May God's curse be upon you and upon your commander (and upon your safe-conduct). You offer us safety while there is no safety for the son of the Messenger of God?!”
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 455. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 146. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 361.
From Medina to Medina: pp. 381-382.

events.title: The Request by Imam Husayn (PBUH) to Delay the Battle
events.text: On the afternoon of Tasu'a, the Imam (PBUH) obtained a respite of one more night in order to postpone the battle. When Umar ibn Sa'd readied the army to fight the Imam (PBUH) and it became clear that they intended to fight, the Hazrat told his brother Abbas (PBUH) to obtain one more night's respite. At first they did not accept, but later they agreed to wait one night.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 455. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 146. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 392.
Manaqib of Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 107.

events.title: The Arrival of Fresh Troops in Karbala
events.text: On this day a well-equipped army arrived in Karbala from Kufa on Ibn Ziyad's orders, and Shimr brought Ibn Ziyad's letter.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 455. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 146.

events.title: Imam Husayn's (PBUH) Address to His Companions
events.text: On the afternoon of this day Imam Husayn (PBUH) delivered a sermon among his companions, and the companions declared their loyalty.
sources: Manaqib of Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 107.

events.title: The Words of the Imam (PBUH) with His Household and Companions
events.text: On this night Imam Husayn (PBUH) gathered his companions and household and spoke some words to them. The gist of the Hazrat's words was: I have lifted my pledge of allegiance from you and left you free to depart wherever you wish. After the Hazrat's words, the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) and the companions expressed words of loyalty and devotion to him.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 147. Wasilat al-Darayn: pp. 298-299.

events.title: The Words of Zaynab al-Kubra (PBUH) with Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text: It was on this night that Zaynab al-Kubra (PBUH) heard the verses “Ya dahr uffin laka min khalil...” (O time, shame on you as a friend...) from her brother Imam Husayn (PBUH), and when she realized that tomorrow would be the day of the Hazrat's martyrdom, she said: “If only death had annihilated me and I had not seen this day.” Then she struck her face and fainted. The Imam (PBUH) revived his dear and honored sister and spoke some words to her.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: p. 149. Wasilat al-Darayn: pp. 302-303.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 61 AH, which was a Saturday or Monday, our master and lord Hazrat Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (PBUH), at the age of 58 (or 56 or 57), after the noon prayer, was martyred oppressed, thirsty and hungry in the land of Karbala. This day is the day of blood raining from the sky, and it is the day on which the martyrdom of the Ahl al-Bayt and companions of Imam Husayn (PBUH) took place.
On this day four thousand angels came down to the land of Karbala to help him, and since they were not given permission, they remain weeping by his grave until the uprising of Hazrat Mahdi (PBUH). On this day, abstaining from eating and drinking, especially from delicious foods, is appropriate.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 133. A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 420. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2, p. 40. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 3. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 25. Kafi: vol. 2, p. 484. Tahdhib of Shaykh Tusi: vol. 6, p. 42. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 306. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 2, p. 5. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 594. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 712. Maqatil al-Talibiyyin: p. 78.
Zad al-Ma'ad: pp. 306-307.
Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 3. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 25.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Habib ibn Mazahir al-Asadi al-Kufi
The Martyrdom of Muslim ibn Awsajah
The Martyrdom of Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi
The Martyrdom of Jawn, Freedman of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari
The Martyrdom of Wahb's Wife at the Hands of Rustam, Shimr's Servant
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 288.

events.title: The Martyrdom of the One Who Most Resembled the Messenger of God (SAWW), Ali Akbar (PBUH), the Eldest Son of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH)
The Martyrdom of Qasim ibn al-Hasan (PBUH)
The Martyrdom of Abdullah ibn al-Hasan (PBUH)
The Martyrdom of the Luminous Moon of the Banu Hashim, Hazrat Abbas ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH)
The Martyrdom of Our Master the Infant, Bab al-Hawa'ij Ali Asghar (PBUH)
The Arrival of Dhuljanah, with Blood-Stained Mane and Forelock, at the Tents of the Fatimid Women to Bring the News of the Hazrat's Martyrdom
The Mourning, Wailing and Weeping of the Women of the Sanctuary over Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH) and His Children, Relatives and Companions
The Plundering of Belongings from the Tents of Imam Husayn (PBUH)
The Flight of the Fatimid and Alawid Women into the Desert After the Martyrdom of Their Master and Lord Aba Abdillah (PBUH)
The Stripping of Clothes, Armor, Etc. from the Pure Bodies of the Martyrs of Karbala
The Severing of the Pure Heads of Imam Husayn (PBUH), the Ahl al-Bayt and His Companions
The Burning of the Tents of the Family of God, the Children of the Messenger of God, Ali al-Murtada and Fatima al-Zahra (PBUH)
The Martyrdom of Young Girls Beside the Tents
Weeping and Mourning for Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH)
events.text:
And the mourning of earth and time, throne and heaven, jinn and humans, angels and wild beasts for that Hazrat.
On this day an angel cried out: O oppressive nation who killed the progeny of your Prophet, may God not grant you to reach Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, p. 218. Wasa'il al-Shi'a: vol. 4, p. 213.

events.title: The Pure Head of Imam Husayn (PBUH) in Kufa
events.text: On the afternoon of Ashura, the pure and luminous head of Imam Husayn (PBUH) was sent to Kufa by the accursed Khawli ibn Yazid al-Asbahi and Humayd ibn Muslim al-Azdi.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 470. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 401. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 155.

events.title: The Roots of Every Plant Pulled from the Ground Turning Bloody, Because of the Great Calamity of That Day
The Killing of Ibn Ziyad
events.text:
In the year 67 AH, on the day of Ashura, Ibn Ziyad met the apparent recompense for his deeds and was killed on the order of Mukhtar. Husayn ibn Numayr and a group of the killers of Imam Husayn (PBUH) were also killed along with Ibn Ziyad.
The accursed Ibn Ziyad was killed by Ibrahim, son of Malik al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i, and his filthy head was sent to Mukhtar. Mukhtar in turn sent his head to Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH). When Ibn Ziyad's head was brought in, the Hazrat was eating a meal. So he performed a prostration of thanks and said: “On the day they brought us in before Ibn Ziyad, he was eating. I asked God not to let me leave this world until I saw his head at my own meal, just as the head of my honored father was before him while he ate. May God reward Mukhtar with goodness, for he avenged us.” Then the Hazrat said to his companions: Everyone give thanks.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 90. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Dhu al-Hijjah, p. 424. Isti'ab: vol. 1, p. 396. Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: vol. 8, p. 310.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 215.

events.title: The Uprising of Hazrat Mahdi (PBUH)
events.text: According to one narration, Hazrat Baqiyyatullah al-A'zam Hujjat ibn al-Hasan al-Askari (may our souls be sacrificed for him) will rise on this day.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 286. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 190.

events.title: The Death of Umm Salamah
events.text:
On this day in the year 62-63 AH, Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (SAWW), passed away. Her name was Hind, her father was Abi Umayya, and her mother was Atika, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib. Her first husband was her maternal cousin Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad ibn al-Mughira. When he was honored with Islam, he and his wife Umm Salamah migrated to Abyssinia. After returning from Abyssinia, as a result of a wound he had received in the Battle of Uhud, he was martyred after some time.
Salamah, Umar, Zaynab and Durra were her children; and Umar took part in all the wars of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and for a time was governor of Bahrain on his behalf.
After Umm Salamah's waiting period ('idda) following her husband's death ended, Abu Bakr and Umar each separately went to ask for her hand, but Umm Salamah did not accept. In the fourth year of the Hijra the Prophet (SAWW) asked for her hand and Umm Salamah accepted, and she said to her son Umar ibn Abi Salamah: Conduct the marriage contract.
When Aisha saw that the Prophet (SAWW) had taken Umm Salamah in marriage, she was extremely upset, since Umm Salamah was of rare beauty. Aisha said to Hafsa: How beautiful Umm Salamah is! She did not believe it until she saw Umm Salamah. For this reason the jealousy of these two toward Umm Salamah was very great.
Umm Salamah has virtues that distinguished her from the other wives of the Prophet (SAWW) - except Khadija al-Kubra (PBUH):
1- Umm Salamah repeatedly advised Aisha, urging her to follow Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), but she would not accept; she recounted that Hazrat's virtues and merits to Aisha, but she would not accept, until she sent her son Umar ibn Abi Salamah with a letter to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) in which she reported that Aisha had set out toward Basra....
2- Umm Salamah testified that Aisha was an enemy of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH).
3- Umm Salamah heard that one of her freedmen had cursed Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). She summoned that person and recounted to him so many of the virtues and merits of Ali (PBUH) that she had heard from the Prophet (SAWW), until he repented.
4- Umm Salamah denied the hadith “We, the company of the prophets, leave no inheritance...” - which Abu Bakr falsely attributed to the Messenger of God (SAWW).
5- When Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) set out for the Battle of the Camel, Umm Salamah sent her son Umar ibn Abi Salamah to help him, and sent that Hazrat the message: “If the Prophet (SAWW) had not commanded his wives to stay in their houses, I would have come and would not have fallen short in supporting and helping you.”
6- After the passing of Khadija al-Kubra (PBUH), the care of Hazrat Zahra (PBUH) was with Fatima bint Asad (PBUH). After the passing of Fatima bint Asad, this important duty was entrusted to Umm Salamah by the Prophet (SAWW), and Aisha was extremely angry about this. Umm Salamah would say: “People think I am the teacher of Fatima (PBUH)! By God, that Hazrat is my teacher!”
7- One day the Prophet (SAWW) called for a sheep's skin, said some things, and Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) wrote them down. Then he gave that skin to Umm Salamah and said: “Whoever gives you such-and-such signs after me, hand this skin over to him.” Those three people did not have those signs, and during the apparent caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), Umm Salamah handed that skin over to that Hazrat - who possessed all the signs.
8- When Imam Husayn (PBUH) was setting out from Medina to Mecca, Umm Salamah came and, with great sorrow, recounted the news of that Hazrat's martyrdom which she had heard from the Prophet (SAWW). Imam Husayn (PBUH) miraculously showed the place of his martyrdom and the burial place of himself and his companions, etc. Then he gave Umm Salamah some of the soil of that pure spot, and it remained with her until the day of Ashura, when Umm Salamah saw the Prophet (SAWW) in a dream, dusty and with disheveled hair, and said: O Messenger of God, what is this state I see you in? He said: “O Umm Salamah, they killed my Husayn, and last night I was digging graves for him and his companions.”
When she woke from sleep, she saw that the soil which the Prophet (SAWW) and Imam Husayn (PBUH) had given her had turned into fresh blood.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 215.
Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 2, pp. 283-305.

events.title: Sham-e Ghariban (the Evening of the Bereaved) in Karbala
events.text:
The first night of mourning and grief of the family of the Prophet (SAWW) after the martyrdom of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH). A night darker than blackness! A heart-burning night in which the bitterest moments passed over the family of Imam Husayn (PBUH).
Can the suffering, burning pain and calamity of the Hazrat's survivors on that night be described, or even imagined? Does anyone grasp how much and in what manner the blood-weeping eyes of the aunt of Imam Zaman (PBUH) and the Ahl al-Bayt wept for that Hazrat? Can one picture how the burning moans and cries of those dear ones were?
With what tongue and what words can one express the broken hearts, the wounded hearts, the cries and songs of the nightingales with singed wings of the Prophetic and Alawid rose garden, and the burning hearts of the orphans and the Husayni women?
It is the evening of the bereaved! The orphaned children who had a father last night, and the unprotected women who last night had a guardian and a home - tonight, with a burned nest and grief-stricken hearts, without their master Hazrat Aba Abdillah (PBUH), what do they do? How great is the difference between these two nights: the night of Ashura and the eleventh night! Last night what a chief they had! Last night who guarded the tents? Last night who was in the tents? Today, however, their blessed body lies headless on the ground! That night who had charge of the Alawid and Fatimid women? What was the state of Zaynab al-Kubra (PBUH) that night? On one side caring for the proof of God, Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH), the wives and the orphans of her brother, and on the other searching for the missing girls!! All this in a land where the body of her brother and her dear ones lay on the ground in that condition!
Ah, what a night that night was, and what a state the daughter of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) was in. “Salamun ala qalbi Zaynab al-sabur wa lisaniha al-shakur” (Peace be upon the patient heart of Zaynab and her thankful tongue).
events.section: Night of the Eleventh of Muharram
sources: From the Ziyarat of Hazrat Zaynab (PBUH).

events.title: The Head of Imam Husayn (PBUH) in Khawli's Oven
events.text: The eleventh night is the night when the pure head of Imam Husayn (PBUH) was in the oven of Khawli's house, while the luminosity of that head lit up the space.
events.section: Night of the Eleventh of Muharram
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 155-156.

events.title: The Departure of the Caravan of Captives from Karbala
events.text: The accursed Umar ibn Sa'd stayed in Karbala until noon on the eleventh, performed the prayer over those killed from his army and buried them. When the day passed its midpoint, he gave the order, and they seated the daughters of the Prophet (SAWW) on unsaddled camels and also seated Sayyid Sajjad (PBUH) on a camel, bound in an iron collar. When they were taken past the killing-ground and the eyes of the women fell on the pure body of Imam Husayn (PBUH), they struck their faces and raised cries of lamentation and wailing.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 184. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 156. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 2, p. 90.

events.title: The Convening of Ibn Ziyad's Assembly
events.text: On the eleventh day Umar ibn Sa'd came to Kufa. Ibn Ziyad gave general permission for the people to attend the assembly. Then the pure head of Imam Husayn (PBUH) was placed before him, and he looked at it, smiled, and with a stick he held in his hand he committed insolence against it.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 471.

events.title: The Departure of the Household of Imam Husayn (PBUH) Toward Kufa
events.text: On the afternoon of the eleventh, the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) were taken toward Kufa in a state of captivity. They set out near sunset and reached Kufa at night. Therefore those bereaved and afflicted noble ones were kept until morning outside the gates of Kufa. In the morning the accursed Umar ibn Sa'd left Kufa and, like a commander pleased with his conquests, entered Kufa together with the captives.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 471.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 204.

events.title: The Burial of the Martyrs of Karbala
events.text: The day of the burial of the pure bodies of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH) and the Ahl al-Bayt and companions of that Hazrat, by Imam Sajjad (PBUH) with the help of a group of the Banu Asad.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 470. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. of Muharram, p. 61. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Tatimmat Muharram, p. 132.

events.title: The Entry of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) into Kufa
events.text:
The twelfth day is the day of the entry of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) into Kufa in captivity. On this day Ibn Ziyad ordered that no one had the right to leave his house with weapons, and he assigned ten thousand horsemen and foot soldiers over all the alleys and the bazaar so that none of the Shi'a of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) would make a move. Then he ordered that the heads that were in Kufa be brought back and made to move ahead of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), and that they be brought into the city together and paraded through the alleys and the bazaar.
Seeing the pitiful state of the descendants of the Prophet (SAWW), the heads on spears, and the women and ladies in uncovered howdahs, the people raised their voices in weeping. Zaynab al-Kubra, Umm Kulthum, Fatima bint al-Husayn and Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUT), in turn, with burning livers and aching hearts, delivered sermons, and a number of the army, seeing this situation, regretted what they had done - but when it was very late!!
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 204. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. of Muharram, p. 25.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 205.

events.title: The Day of the Martyrdom of Hazrat Sajjad (PBUH)
events.text: According to one view, the martyrdom of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH) took place on this day in the year 94 AH, at the age of 57; another view is the 25th of Muharram, which will come later.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 3.

events.title: The Captives of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) in Ibn Ziyad's Assembly
events.text: After the captives and the sacred heads of the martyrs were paraded in Kufa, Ibn Ziyad sat in his palace and ordered that the pure head of Imam Husayn (PBUH) be placed before him. Then the women and children of that Hazrat, together with Imam Sajjad (PBUH) - bound with ropes - were brought into the assembly and kept standing before that accursed one's throne. Meanwhile, the courtiers of that accursed one stood watching.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 4, p. 63. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Tatimmat Muharram, p. 256.

events.title: The Captives of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) in the Prison of Kufa
events.text: After Ibn Ziyad's ominous assembly, the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) were taken, in shackles and chains, into the prison of Kufa.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. of Muharram, p. 94. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Tatimmat Muharram, p. 263.

events.title: The News of the Martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH) in Medina and Syria
events.text: Ibn Ziyad wrote letters to Medina and Syria and spread the news of the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH).
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. of Muharram, p. 96. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Tatimmat Muharram, p. 263.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Abdullah ibn Afif
events.text:
Abdullah ibn Afif al-Azdi was a noble man among the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) who had lost both his eyes in the battles of the Camel and Siffin. He was therefore occupied with worship.
When he heard that the son of Ziyad, the accursed, was attributing lying to Amir al-Mu'minin and Imam Husayn (PBUH), he rose from among the crowd and said: Be silent, O son of Marjana, the liar is you and your father who gave you this position. O enemy of God! You kill the children of the Prophet (SAWW) and speak like this on the pulpits of the believers? The agents wanted to seize him, but with the help of his tribe he went home; later, however, they came and surrounded his house. After his valiant acts and those of his daughter, he was arrested and, as he had asked of God, was martyred at the hands of the worst of creation, namely Ibn Ziyad.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 4, p. 80; pp. 87-88.

events.title: Sending the Pure Heads of the Martyrs Toward Syria
events.text: According to some accounts, on this day the pure heads of the Ahl al-Bayt of infallibility and purity (PBUT) were sent toward Syria. Of course, afterwards the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) rejoined the pure heads to the bodies.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Tatimmat Muharram, p. 281.

events.title: The Departure of the Karbala Caravan Toward Syria
events.text: On this day the household of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH) were sent from Kufa toward Syria. The non-Hashimite women among the supporters of Imam Husayn (PBUH) who had been captured in Karbala were released from captivity before Ibn Ziyad through the intercession of their relatives and tribes, and only the Hashimite women were taken to Syria into captivity.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 4, p. 114.
Absar al-Ayn fi Ansar al-Husayn (PBUH): p. 133.

events.title: The Burial of Jawn's Body in Karbala
events.text:
Ten days after the event of Ashura, a group of the Banu Asad found the noble body of Jawn, the servant of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, with his face luminous and his body fragrant, and then they buried him.
Jawn was a man whom Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) bought for 150 dinars and gave to Abu Dharr. When Abu Dharr was exiled to Rabadha, this servant went to Rabadha to help him, and after the passing of Abu Dharr he returned to Medina and was in the service of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), until after that Hazrat's martyrdom he came into the service of Imam Mujtaba (PBUH) and then of Imam Husayn (PBUH), and accompanied him from Medina to Mecca and from Mecca to Karbala. When the fighting intensified on the day of Ashura, he came to Imam Husayn (PBUH) and asked permission to go to the battlefield and defend the sanctuary of wilayah and imamate. The Hazrat said: You were with us on this journey in hope of well-being and safety! Now do not afflict yourself for our sake.
Jawn threw himself on the blessed feet of Imam Husayn (PBUH), kissed them and said: O son of the Messenger of God, when you were in comfort and ease I lived off your table, and now that you are afflicted with calamity, should I abandon you?
Jawn thought to himself: Who am I, and who is this household?! So he said: My master, my smell is bad, I have no family nobility, and my color is black. O Aba Abdillah, kindly make me a dweller of Paradise so that my smell becomes pleasant, I gain family nobility, and I become honored (white-faced). No, my master, I will not be separated from you until my black blood is mixed with the blood of you, the family. Jawn spoke and wept so much that Imam Husayn (PBUH) wept and gave permission.
Although Jawn was a 90-year-old man, the children in the sanctuary were very fond of him. He came to the side of the tents to say farewell and ask forgiveness, and the cries of the children rose and they gathered around him. He quieted each one with a word and sent them to the tents, and like an angry lion he turned toward that impure people. He fought conspicuously until they surrounded him and inflicted many wounds on him. When he fell to the ground, Imam Husayn (PBUH) took his head into his lap and wept aloud, and passed his blessed hand over Jawn's head and face and said: “Allahumma bayyid wajhahu wa tayyib rihahu wahshurhu ma'a Muhammad wa Al Muhammad (PBUT)” - O God, whiten his face, make his scent pleasant, and raise him with the household of infallibility (PBUT).
By the blessing of the Hazrat's prayer, the servant's face shone like the full moon and the scent of perfume reached the nose from him. So when they found his body after ten days, his face was luminous and his scent fragrant.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 311.
Wasilat al-Darayn fi Ansar al-Husayn (PBUH): p. 115.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Imam Sajjad (PBUH)
events.text:
In the year 94 AH according to the well-known view, or 95 AH, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH), at the age of 57, was martyred by means of a coat of armor that Walid ibn Abd al-Malik or Hisham - may God curse them both - gave to that Hazrat. This was after he had spent 34 or 35 years after the Karbala event weeping over the heart-melting calamities of the martyrdom of his father, brothers, uncle and relatives and the captivity of his aunts and sisters.
Imam Baqir (PBUH) prepared his body and buried him in Baqi', beside the grave of his oppressed uncle Hazrat Mujtaba (PBUH). The year of that Hazrat's martyrdom was called “Sanat al-Fuqaha'” (the Year of the Jurists) because of the many deaths of jurists and scholars. There are also other views on his martyrdom: 12 Muharram, 18 Muharram, 19 Muharram, 2 Safar.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 26. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 315. Al-'Udad al-Qawiyya: p. 315. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 328. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 594. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 729. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 165. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 59, p. 199.
Usul al-Kafi: vol. 2, p. 491.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 2, p. 37. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 4, p. 287. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 218.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Muthallath
events.text: In the year 146 AH, Ali ibn Hasan ibn Hasan ibn Hasan ibn Ali (PBUH), at the age of 45, in the prison of Mansur - where night and day could not be told apart - was martyred while in prostration, with shackles and chains on his hands and feet.
sources: Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 4, p. 289. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, pp. 259-260.

events.title: The Death of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman
events.text:
Hudhayfah was among the great companions of the Prophet (SAWW) and among the special companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). Hudhayfah's father was mistakenly killed by one of the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud.
Hudhayfah was one of the seven people who performed the prayer over Siddiqa Tahira (Fatima al-Zahra) (PBUH). He knew the hypocrite companions - the hypocrites who, after Ghadir Khumm, plotted to kill the Prophet (SAWW) and wanted, on the way back from Ghadir Khumm, on a road that passed through the mountain, to frighten the Hazrat's camel so that it would bolt and the Hazrat would fall into the valley and be killed. But Gabriel conveyed this plan to the Prophet's blessed ear.
When the Prophet (SAWW) reached the intended place, the hypocrites, with their faces covered, each threw down from above a container filled with pebbles and began shouting and bellowing. But Ammar had taken hold of the camel's halter and Hudhayfah was also beside the Hazrat, and in the end the plan of those blind-hearted ones came to nothing.
The Prophet (SAWW) introduced those hypocrites to Hudhayfah, and they were: the first, the second and the third, Abu Ubayda, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Salim, Mu'awiya, Amr ibn al-As, Talha, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mughira ibn Shu'ba and Abu Hurayra; Hudhayfah memorized them all. It was for this reason that the usurpers of the caliphate, after that event, feared Hudhayfah, lest he introduce them to the people.
Therefore, whenever Hudhayfah attended someone's funeral, others understood that the deceased had been among the hypocrites. The interesting point was that the second, to cover up his own hypocrisy and exonerate himself, would ask Hudhayfah: “If this person is one of the hypocrites, tell me so that I do not pray over him”!
This noble man passed away in Mada'in forty days after the apparent caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). Before his passing he entrusted his sons Safwan and Sa'id with a will to always remain attached to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and they acted on their father's will until they were martyred in the Battle of Siffin.
sources: Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 120. Usd al-Ghaba: vol. 1, p. 391.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 212. Al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 4, p. 308. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, p. 242.

events.title: The Exile of Imam Jawad (PBUH) to Baghdad
events.text: In the year 220 AH, Imam Jawad (PBUH) was exiled from Medina to Baghdad on the order of Mu'tasim.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 295.

events.title: The Entry of the Captives of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) into Baalbek
events.text: According to one account, the entry of the captives of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) into the city of Baalbek, and the people of that city welcoming the spear-bearers with sugar, sawiq (roasted-barley flour), provisions and fodder, took place on this day; seeing this scene, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (PBUH) cursed them.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 332.

events.title: The Arrival of the Caravan of Captives in Syria
events.text: On this day the captives of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) reached the outskirts of Syria. Ibrahim ibn Talha ibn Abdullah came forward and approached Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH), and revealed the grudges he had stored in his chest from the wounds of the swords of the Battle of the Camel, and said to the Hazrat: Did you see who prevailed? The Hazrat said: If you want to know who prevails, wait until the time of prayer and recite the adhan and iqama; then you will know whose renown remains until the Resurrection.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Muharram and Safar, p. 336.

events.title: The Writing of the Accursed Scroll
events.text:
In this month in the year 11 AH the second accursed scroll was written and was signed by the hypocrites.
Its content was that they would not let the caliphate and imamate of the Muslims after the Prophet (SAWW) go to Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), and on that basis they prepared the preliminaries and groundwork for usurping the caliphate and obtaining allegiance from that Hazrat by any means possible. With the writing of that scroll they laid the foundation of oppression and tyranny against the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), and as Imam Sadiq (PBUH) said: “Idha kutiba al-kitab qutila al-Husayn (PBUH)” (When the scroll was written, Husayn (PBUH) was martyred).
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 28, p. 104.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 24, p. 366; vol. 28, p. 123; vol. 31, p. 635. Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: vol. 4, p. 616. Ta'wil al-Ayat: vol. 2, p. 672.

events.title: The Death of Maria al-Qibtiyya
events.text:
In the month of Muharram in the year 15 AH (or 16 AH) Maria al-Qibtiyya passed away.
Maria was the daughter of Sham'un the Copt, who together with her sister Sirin and a eunuch who was Maria's brother named Mabur, and a thousand mithqals of gold, twenty garments of silk, a donkey named Ya'fur and a mule named Duldul, was sent in the seventh year by the king of Alexandria as a gift to the Messenger of God (SAWW).
The Prophet (SAWW) chose Maria as his wife and prepared a house for her in the district of “Aliya” - which is called “Mashrabat Umm Ibrahim” - and God granted the Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) to that Hazrat from this lady.
Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) expressed great joy at the birth of Ibrahim (PBUH) and would serve them, and for this reason Aisha was very upset and resentful toward Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH). It is reported from Aisha that she said: “I was jealous of Maria, because she was a very beautiful woman.” In the end this jealousy led her to slander Maria, and a verse was revealed condemning this act of Aisha, which is explained in detail in Shi'a and Sunni exegeses. Maria passed away in Medina after the Prophet (SAWW).
sources: Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 2, p. 342. Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: vol. 5, p. 326.
Sharh Nahj al-Balagha of Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 9, p. 195.
Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 2, p. 342. Al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: vol. 8, p. 213. Al-Isaba: p. 311.

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
